description: Assess a vendor's security posture from questionnaire design through response collection, control evaluation, risk rating, contract requirements, and a final assessment report.

steps.description: Design a security questionnaire and evidence request list scoped to the vendor and the services they provide.

inputs.name: vendor-profile
inputs.desc: Vendor name, services provided, data accessed, and integration points.

inputs.name: assessment-scope
inputs.desc: Depth of review, applicable frameworks, and the sensitivity of data in play.

outputs.name: security-questionnaire
outputs.desc: Set of control questions grouped by domain and weighted by relevance to the scope.

outputs.name: evidence-request-list
outputs.desc: Supporting documents and artifacts the vendor must supply to back their answers.

process: Map the vendor services and data access to the control domains that apply.
Select or tailor questions for each domain and drop questions that do not fit the scope.
Weight questions by the data sensitivity and the blast radius of the integration.
List the evidence needed to verify each high-weight answer, such as policies, reports, and certificates.

steps.description: Collect vendor answers and supporting evidence, track outstanding items, and flag incomplete or inconsistent responses.

inputs.name: security-questionnaire
inputs.desc: The scoped question set issued to the vendor.

inputs.name: evidence-request-list
inputs.desc: The documents and artifacts requested alongside the questionnaire.

outputs.name: completed-responses
outputs.desc: Vendor answers keyed to each question with a status of complete, partial, or missing.

outputs.name: submitted-evidence
outputs.desc: Received documents linked to the questions they support, with gaps noted.

process: Issue the questionnaire and evidence request to the vendor contact with a due date.
Record each answer and attach submitted evidence to the question it supports.
Track outstanding questions and missing documents and send follow-up reminders.
Flag answers that conflict with the evidence or with other answers for later review.

steps.description: Evaluate collected responses and evidence against control expectations and record findings where controls fall short.

inputs.name: completed-responses
inputs.desc: Vendor answers with completion status.

inputs.name: submitted-evidence
inputs.desc: Supporting documents linked to each answer.

outputs.name: control-evaluation
outputs.desc: Per-control rating of met, partially met, or not met with the evidence that supports the rating.

outputs.name: finding-list
outputs.desc: Specific control shortfalls with a short description and the affected data or system.

process: Compare each answer and its evidence to the expected control outcome.
Rate each control as met, partially met, or not met and cite the evidence.
Record a finding for every control that is partially met or not met.
Note where missing evidence prevents a rating and mark it for follow-up.

steps.description: Rate the overall vendor risk from the control findings, the data exposure, and the likelihood and impact of each shortfall.

inputs.name: control-evaluation
inputs.desc: Per-control ratings with supporting evidence.

inputs.name: finding-list
inputs.desc: The specific control shortfalls identified.

outputs.name: risk-rating
outputs.desc: Overall vendor risk tier with per-finding severity scores.

outputs.name: risk-justification
outputs.desc: Written rationale linking each score to the finding, the data exposure, and the likely impact.

process: Score each finding by likelihood and by impact on the data it touches.
Roll the finding scores into an overall vendor risk tier.
Write the rationale that ties each score to the evidence and the data exposure.
Call out any single finding severe enough to block the engagement on its own.

steps.description: Translate the risk rating and findings into contract security requirements and conditions the vendor must meet before or during the engagement.

inputs.name: risk-rating
inputs.desc: Overall vendor risk tier with per-finding severity.

inputs.name: finding-list
inputs.desc: The specific control shortfalls to address.

outputs.name: contract-security-requirements
outputs.desc: Clauses and obligations to add to the agreement, such as audit rights, breach notice, and control commitments.

outputs.name: remediation-conditions
outputs.desc: Findings the vendor must fix with target dates and the proof required to close each one.

process: Map each high-severity finding to a contract clause or an obligation.
Set audit rights, breach notice terms, and control commitments sized to the risk tier.
Define remediation conditions with target dates and the proof needed to close them.
Mark which conditions must be met before signing and which may run during the term.

steps.description: Compile the control evaluation, risk rating, and contract requirements into a vendor assessment report with an executive summary and a go or no-go recommendation.

inputs.name: control-evaluation
inputs.desc: Per-control ratings and findings.

inputs.name: risk-rating
inputs.desc: Overall vendor risk tier and per-finding severity.

inputs.name: contract-security-requirements
inputs.desc: Clauses and obligations to add to the agreement.

outputs.name: vendor-assessment-report
outputs.desc: Full report with scope, control results, findings, risk rating, and contract requirements.

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary with the risk tier, the top findings, and a go or no-go recommendation.

process: Assemble the scope, control results, findings, and risk rating into one report.
Attach the contract requirements and the remediation conditions.
Write a one-page summary with the risk tier and the top findings.
State a go or no-go recommendation and the conditions that would change it.

description: Design a security awareness training program from audience analysis through learning objectives, content development, delivery scheduling, effectiveness measurement, and a program report.

steps.description: Analyze the workforce to segment the audience by role, access, and the security risks each group is most exposed to.

inputs.name: workforce-profile
inputs.desc: Roles, departments, access levels, and locations across the workforce.

inputs.name: risk-focus-areas
inputs.desc: Threats and incidents the program must address, such as phishing, data handling, and account security.

outputs.name: audience-segments
outputs.desc: Groups of staff that share a role, access level, and risk exposure.

outputs.name: role-risk-map
outputs.desc: Mapping of each segment to the security risks it is most likely to face.

process: Group the workforce by role, access level, and work setting.
Map each group to the threats and incidents it is most exposed to.
Flag high-access and high-exposure groups that need deeper coverage.
Record any language, location, or schedule constraints that affect delivery.

steps.description: Set measurable learning objectives and a topic outline for each audience segment based on its risk exposure.

inputs.name: audience-segments
inputs.desc: The staff groups to train.

inputs.name: role-risk-map
inputs.desc: The security risks mapped to each segment.

outputs.name: learning-objectives
outputs.desc: Measurable objectives per segment stating what staff should be able to recognize or do.

outputs.name: topic-outline
outputs.desc: Ordered list of topics and sub-topics that cover the objectives for each segment.

process: Turn each mapped risk into a measurable objective for the segment it affects.
State what staff should be able to recognize, avoid, or report after the training.
Order the topics so that foundational ideas come before segment-specific ones.
Set the minimum passing standard for each objective.

steps.description: Develop training modules and assessment items that meet the learning objectives for each audience segment.

inputs.name: learning-objectives
inputs.desc: The measurable objectives to meet.

inputs.name: topic-outline
inputs.desc: The ordered topics to cover.

outputs.name: training-modules
outputs.desc: Short lessons with examples and scenarios keyed to each objective.

outputs.name: assessment-items
outputs.desc: Quiz and exercise items that test each objective against its passing standard.

process: Build a short lesson for each topic with a real-world example or scenario.
Key each lesson to the objective it serves so coverage is traceable.
Write assessment items that test each objective at its passing standard.
Keep the length and reading level suited to each segment.

steps.description: Plan delivery and enrollment so each audience segment receives its modules through a suitable channel on a workable schedule.

inputs.name: training-modules
inputs.desc: The lessons ready for delivery.

inputs.name: audience-segments
inputs.desc: The staff groups and their constraints.

outputs.name: delivery-schedule
outputs.desc: Dates, channels, and durations for delivering each module to each segment.

outputs.name: enrollment-plan
outputs.desc: Assignment of staff to modules with reminders and completion deadlines.

process: Pick a delivery channel for each segment that fits its schedule and setting.
Lay out dates and durations that avoid known blackout periods.
Assign each staff group to its modules with a completion deadline.
Set reminder points and an escalation path for overdue completions.

steps.description: Measure training effectiveness from assessment results and delivery data, and identify where knowledge gaps remain.

inputs.name: assessment-items
inputs.desc: The quiz and exercise items tied to each objective.

inputs.name: delivery-schedule
inputs.desc: The planned delivery with dates and channels.

outputs.name: effectiveness-metrics
outputs.desc: Completion rates, pass rates, and score trends by segment and by objective.

outputs.name: knowledge-gap-report
outputs.desc: Objectives and segments where results fall below the passing standard.

process: Collect completion and pass rates by segment and by objective.
Compare scores against the passing standard set for each objective.
Track score trends across delivery waves to see whether they improve.
List the objectives and segments that still fall short and the likely cause.

steps.description: Compile the effectiveness metrics, gaps, and delivery record into a program report with an executive summary and next-cycle recommendations.

inputs.name: effectiveness-metrics
inputs.desc: Completion, pass, and trend data by segment and objective.

inputs.name: knowledge-gap-report
inputs.desc: Where results fall short of the passing standard.

inputs.name: delivery-schedule
inputs.desc: The delivery record with dates and channels.

outputs.name: training-program-report
outputs.desc: Full report with objectives, delivery record, results, and remaining gaps.

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary of reach, results, and recommendations for the next cycle.

process: Assemble the objectives, delivery record, and results into one report.
Highlight the segments and objectives that met and missed their standard.
Write a one-page summary of reach and results for leadership.
Recommend changes to content, audience, or schedule for the next cycle.
